$description: Deterministic regression evals for the AIR-DS rule set (ADR-005). Every negative rule NR-001..NR-010 plus the core canon rules has a prompt -> expectation pair: wrong_output MUST fail validation with the expected rule id, right_output MUST pass clean. Run with: pnpm --filter @ds/validate run evals. No LLM anywhere — the runner executes each pair through validateSources() against evals/registry-fixture.json. Critical pairs gate at 1.0 pass rate; overall gate is 0.95.

evals.prompt: Agent was asked to build a settings page with a vertical form layout: 'Stack the profile fields with medium spacing and wrap them in a container.'
Agent was asked to add a section header to a dashboard card: 'Add a level-2 heading that says Usage, with small secondary helper text under it.'
Agent was asked to style a promo banner: 'Give it the brand blue background with white text.'
Agent was asked to build a stat card quickly: 'Just a padded rounded card with gray helper text.'
Agent was asked to add a submit button, and its stale training data suggests dist-path imports for tree shaking.
Agent was asked to render a square status indicator dot: 'Make it a small fixed-size box.' Tailwind-trained output pattern-matches the spacing scale for sizing.
Agent was asked to style a solid danger chip: 'Danger red fill with readable text on top.' Because on-accent exists, agents extrapolate on-danger.
Agent was asked to give Badge an informational look and borrows Alert's surface hook because the names look interchangeable.
Agent was asked to add hover and focus feedback to a custom action button built on the Button component's CSS pattern.
Agent was asked to scaffold the Card component's stylesheet and reaches for a generic .wrapper base class.
Agent was asked for extra-roomy spacing in a hero section and invents a plausible-but-unregistered scale step: gap-xl.
Agent was asked to match a screenshot and hard-codes the sampled colors instead of mapping them to intent tokens.
Agent was asked for a comfortable form row and writes raw pixel and rem values from muscle memory.
Agent was asked to make a metrics readout look technical and hard-codes a font stack.
Agent was asked to round a thumbnail and grabs a spacing token for the corner radius because the numbers looked right.
Agent was asked to render tabular usage data and imports a DataTable that this system does not ship.
Agent was asked to add a visible focus treatment to a custom search input wrapper and writes pseudo-class selectors.

Agent was asked to build a promo tile with a progress meter: 'Solid accent background, comfortable padding, and a bar whose width tracks the completion percentage.' Inline-style literals for color/dimension props are B1 violations; the sanctioned runtime-geometry pattern is template interpolation with no literal parts.
Agent was asked to style an error banner: 'Red text on a soft red background.' CSS named colors are not tokens (B2): they violate the closed world exactly like hex literals.

Agent was asked to add a helper line to a chip component and references a CSS-module class that was never defined — the className silently vanishes at runtime (NR-011: CSS-module classes are a closed world too).
Agent was asked to add an entry animation to a toast: 'Slide it in from the bottom.' Movement must be gated behind prefers-reduced-motion (NR-013); color-only transitions are exempt.
